sections.html:
Marion is the Grant County seat, on the Mississinewa River in north central Indiana. The 2020 census counted 28,310 residents and the 2025 estimate is 28,234. The city peaked at 39,607 people in 1970, and the loss of roughly 11,000 residents still shapes the local housing market. Shrinking cities tend to have houses that change hands slowly, and local buyers inspect closely.

The ZIP codes are 46952 and 46953. The city has a mayor and a nine-member council, six elected by ward and three at large.

Owners of residential rental properties, rooming houses and apartment buildings must register with the Building Department. The requirement began January 1, 2020. Applications go to Marion Building / Code Enforcement at 301 S. Branson St., phone 765-662-9931. The city's rental registration page on cityofmarion.in.gov has the form.

Did tenants ever live in the house you are selling? Check that the registration is current first. Straightening that out before a buyer's title company asks is simpler than doing it mid-closing.

A 2018 city ordinance sets minimum standards for every building in Marion. Owners are expected to keep the exterior sound.

  • Foundations, roofs, gutters, windows, doors, stairs and porches must be maintained.
  • Vacant buildings must be locked and secured, and they can be classified as unsafe.
  • Tarps on a structure are limited to 30 days, and the owner must tell the building department first.
  • Repairs are due within 30 days of a notice, or 15 days for unsafe buildings.
  • Fines run up to $500, and each day counts as a separate offense.

Owners who live outside Indiana must appoint a local agent within 30 miles. The civil penalty for skipping that step is $500 per parcel. An heir living in another state who is holding a Marion rental falls under this rule, and a named agent avoids the penalty.

The Building Commissioner can order a building vacated, sealed, repaired or demolished. An order names the responsible party, the action required and a deadline. Most orders can be appealed to the Marion Board of Public Works and Safety, with hearings held at least 10 days after notice.

Owners get 72 hours of written notice before a routine inspection. Demolition debris cannot stay on the lot for more than three months.

A buyer who purchases a damaged house as-is takes over those obligations. That is a common reason owners of run-down houses pick a cash sale. The repair list, the deadlines and the exposure to fines pass to the new owner, and you skip paying for a roof or foundation job to satisfy a retail buyer's lender.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and the county tax sale
sections.html:
Two installments cover the year, one in spring and one in fall. The statutory dates are May 10 and November 10, and the Treasurer posted May 11 and November 10 for 2026. Bills go out by April 15. Pay at the Treasurer's office, 401 S. Adams Street, 2nd Floor, Marion (weekdays, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.). Phone payments are no longer accepted.

Taxes left unpaid can end in a county tax sale. The 2026 sale was held October 26, and the certified list that year held 672 properties. The minimum bid covers delinquent taxes, current-year taxes, penalties and costs.

For certificates sold in 2026, the redemption period ends October 26, 2027. Redeeming costs 110 percent of the minimum bid within six months and 115 percent after that, plus certain added costs.

Should your house ever land on the list, a sale ahead of the auction is one exit. Paying the full judgment amount pulls a parcel off the sale, and a closing that settles the balance from your proceeds accomplishes that.

sections.h2: Which office do you call for what?
sections.html:
• Rental registration and code questions: Marion Building / Code Enforcement, 301 S. Branson St., 765-662-9931.
  • Tax balance, payment and tax sale lists: Grant County Treasurer, 401 S. Adams Street, 2nd Floor.
  • Deed recording: Grant County Recorder, 401 S. Adams Street, 3rd Floor, (765) 668-6559.

All three county and city offices keep weekday business hours, so make these calls before you pick a closing date. Having a payoff figure and a list of open notices in hand lets you judge any offer against what you will actually net.

Deeds are recorded at the Grant County Recorder, at 401 S. Adams Street, 3rd Floor, phone (765) 668-6559, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Documents prepared in Indiana must include a Social Security number redaction affirmation. Card payments carry a 3.0 percent convenience fee.

Before the deed reaches the auditor, Indiana requires buyer and seller to fill out a sales disclosure form. The title company usually does the filing. Your part is to sign and to make sure each person named on the deed can attend or sign ahead of time.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Marion?
sections.html:
Closing a cash purchase uses the usual Indiana paperwork with no lender in the middle, so there is no appraisal or loan approval to hold things up.

  1. Send us the address and describe the house, mentioning notices, tenants or registration questions.
  2. Read the written offer. Weigh it against listing the house, and say no if it does not suit you.
  3. Pick a title company, which searches the title, turns up liens and checks the tax balance with the Treasurer.
  4. Sign the purchase agreement, then the deed and disclosure form on closing day.
  5. Taxes, liens and a mortgage payoff come out of the proceeds, and you receive whatever remains.

A short folder helps: the deed, a recent mortgage statement, the newest tax bill and any letter from Code Enforcement. When the owner has died, the title company will explain who may sign for the estate.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Marion house with open code notices?
sections.html:
Open notices do not block a sale. The contract should state who deals with each item, and a cash buyer commonly absorbs the repairs. Phone Building / Code Enforcement at 765-662-9931 to see what is recorded against your address, and ask the Grant County Treasurer what you owe today.

Written orders carry the most weight. If a repair clock is already running, say so in your first conversation. A vacate or demolition order changes what any buyer will pay, and raising it early beats having the title search reveal it later. Photos of trouble spots and repair quotes you have collected let the buyer price the house faster.

faqs.q: Do landlords in Marion have to register rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of residential rentals, rooming houses and apartment buildings in city limits register with the Building Department. The rule took effect January 1, 2020.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Grant County?
faqs.a: Half is due in spring and half in fall. The statute says May 10 and November 10, with May 11 and November 10 posted for 2026.

faqs.q: What happens if my Marion house is in the county tax sale?
faqs.a: Properties on the certified list can be sold at auction, but a property is removed if the full judgment amount is paid before the sale. After a sale, owners can redeem within a set period at a stated cost.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marion house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it as-is and take on the repairs. Marion's ordinance sets deadlines and fines for violations, so spell out in the sale terms who handles any open notice.

faqs.q: Can an out-of-state owner sell a Marion house?
faqs.a: Yes. Marion's ordinance asks out-of-state owners to name a local agent within 30 miles, and a title company can coordinate the paperwork.
